title: Acceptance of a deterministic true return
statement: Let $m,d$ be natural numbers, let $\Lambda$ be a type of machine states, let $x$ be a bit string, and let $A$ be a nondeterministic register machine with oracle $\mathcal O$ and guard $G$ on configurations. If, at a state $l\in\Lambda$, the machine executes the deterministic instruction that returns true, and $G$ holds at the configuration with state $l$, register contents $v\colon\mathrm{Fin}(m)\to\mathbb N$, and no result yet, then this initial configuration has guarded terminating semantics with acceptance probability $1$.
hypotheses_covered: $\Lambda$ is a type of machine states
$A$ is a nondeterministic register machine and $\mathcal O$ is its oracle
At $l$, $A$ executes the deterministic instruction returning true
$v$ assigns a natural number to each of the $m$ registers
The guard $G$ holds at the initial live configuration with no result
